newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Privatisation hopes boost ZCCM shares.
newsitem.headline: Privatisation hopes boost ZCCM shares.

text.p: Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines' (ZCCM) shares traded in Paris reached a year high on Wednesday, buoyed by recent significant developments in the programme to privatise the mining conglomerate, analysts said.

The share surged to 30.80 francs on Wednesday -- more than double the price in mid-January -- before retreating to 22 francs in afternoon trade. Back in June the stock had been trading at just 5.13 francs.
"The rise in the value of ZCCM shares is a result of investor confidence about the future of ZCCM," Zambian securities and exchange commission secretary Mumba Kapumpa told Reuters.
"Investors believe that the privatisation of ZCCM is on course," he added.
The privatisation of ZCCM kicked off in January with the acquisition of an 80 percent interest in its Kansanshi mine by the American-based Cyprus Amax Minerals.

A consortium led by Anglo American Corp is due to sign a memorandum of understanding on the development of the Konkola Deep mine later this month while rival South African mining house Anglovaal is expected to sign an option agreement on the development of the Konkola North.

The development of Konkola Deep, which has proven reserves of 344 million tonnes of ore at 3.8 percent copper with high potential for additional findings, is seen as crucial to the future of Zambia's mining industry.
Bids for the sale of other ZCCM units are expected to be opened this month.

The Zambia Privatisation Agency (ZPA) technical director Stewart Cruickshank, said investor confidence in ZCCM had also been boosted by the 1997 budget, which committed the government to a speedy privatisation of the company's units.
"The budget had no shocks and the market sees no impediments to the privatisation of ZCCM," he said.
